results.name: Lats Stretch Elbow on Wall
instructions: Stand facing a wall and place one elbow on it above your head.
Step back slightly and lower your chest toward the floor.
Push your hips back until you feel a stretch along the side of your back.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Keep your back flat.
Breathe into the stretch.
results.description: Lats Stretch Elbow on Wall is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Shoulders.

results.name: Lats Stretch on Wall
instructions: Stand facing a wall and place both hands on it at shoulder height or higher.
Walk your feet back and hinge at your hips.
Lower your chest toward the floor until you feel a stretch under your arms.
Hold and breathe.
tips: Keep your arms straight.
Push your hips back.
results.description: Lats Stretch on Wall is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Chest.

results.name: Lying Bent Knee Cross Glutes Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back with both knees bent and feet flat.
Cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Pull the lower leg toward your chest until you feel a stretch in the glute of the crossed leg.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Keep your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor.
Push the crossed knee away gently for more stretch.
results.description: Lying Bent Knee Cross Glutes Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

results.name: Lying Face Down Quadriceps Stretch
instructions: Lie face down on the floor.
Bend one knee and reach back to hold your ankle or foot.
Gently pull your heel toward your glute until you feel a stretch in the front of your thigh.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Keep your hips pressed into the floor.
Use a strap if you can't reach your foot.
results.description: Lying Face Down Quadriceps Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

results.name: Lying Knee Hugs Lower Back Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back.
Pull both knees toward your chest.
Wrap your arms around your shins and hug them in.
Hold, breathing slowly, and relax your lower back into the floor.
tips: Rock gently side to side for a light massage.
Keep your head on the floor.
results.description: Lying Knee Hugs Lower Back Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Glutes.

results.name: Lying Knee Pull Glutes Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs straight.
Bend one knee and pull it toward the opposite shoulder.
Hold until you feel a stretch in your glute.
Release and switch sides.
tips: Keep the other leg relaxed on the floor.
Breathe deeply.
results.description: Lying Knee Pull Glutes Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back.

results.name: Lying Knees to Floor Lower Back Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and arms out to the sides.
Keeping your shoulders on the floor, lower both knees to one side.
Hold, feeling a stretch in your lower back and side.
Bring your knees back to the centre and lower them to the other side.
tips: Turn your head away from your knees for a deeper stretch.
Move slowly.
results.description: Lying Knees to Floor Lower Back Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Glutes.

results.name: Lying Single Leg Extended on Wall Hamstrings Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back in a doorway or next to a wall.
Place one leg straight up against the wall, the other flat on the floor.
Move closer to the wall until you feel a stretch in the back of the raised leg.
Hold, then switch legs.
tips: Keep both legs straight.
Relax your shoulders and neck.
results.description: Lying Single Leg Extended on Wall Hamstrings Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Calves.

results.name: Resistance Band Assisted Front Rack Stretch
instructions: Stand in the middle of a weight cage with a horizontal bar at chest level. Place the resistance band under your left foot and hold the other end of the band with your left hand.
Bring your left elbow up and rest it on the horizontal bar, allowing your forearm to lean backward. The band should extend down by your shoulder, creating tension.
Slowly allow your forearm to lean back to increase the stretch in your shoulder, keeping your hand close to your shoulder.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then slowly release the tension and switch to the other arm.
tips: Keep your elbow securely on the bar to ensure proper stretch.
Allow your forearm to naturally lean back without forcing the movement.
Keep a relaxed grip on the band to avoid unnecessary tension.
results.description: Resistance Band Assisted Front Rack Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Biceps.

results.name: Revolved Head to Knee
instructions: Sit with one leg extended to the side and the other bent, foot against the inside of the extended thigh.
Turn your torso toward the bent knee.
Side-bend over the extended leg and reach your top arm overhead toward the foot.
Hold, breathing into the side of your body, then switch sides.
tips: Keep your chest open toward the ceiling.
Bend the extended knee slightly if your hamstrings are tight.
results.description: Revolved Head to Knee is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Lats, Adductors.
